newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies rally sharply at close.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies rally sharply at close.

text.p: CME pork belly futures rallied sharply by the close as local short covering turned pices up from early losses and fresh technical buying boosted prices up into buy stops. Hog futures ended mostly lower on concern over live markets early next week, traders said.

Pork bellies ran up to close 1.500 to 1.150 cent a lb higher with March up 1.200 at 81.925 cents after trading as low as 79.550 cents early. Hog futures ended 0.475 cent lower to 0.150 higher with only distant April up and nearby April off most at 74.475 cents.
Early local selling and mixed profit taking in bellies lacked follow through and strong technicals took over.
"Charts point up to 88 to 90 cents, contract highs," said Julia Bussie, livestock and technical analyst for AG Edwards.
She noted that bellies moved up to a 27-week high and touched off buy stops above Thursday's high and again above recent chart resistance.

Traders said profit taking developed early on what seemed to be near-term overbought status. Local and commercial selling was also evident on expectations recent gains in cash bellies would curb demand. But selling lacked follow through and local short covering sparked technical demand.

Slaughter rates likely will recede next week as IBP Inc, as earlier announced, ceases its second shift operations at its Columbus Junction, Iowa plant on Monday. IBP also is planning to end slaughter and most processing operations at its Council Bluffs, Iowa plant on April 24.

Such cutbacks sparked ideas of tighter fresh belly supplies in the near term which could spark more competition among storing interests that are hedging again the board. The CME future board currently is holding a premium to cash, sources noted.

R.J. O'Brien traded both sides with their commercial interests selling and funds buying. LIT division of First Options also bought late with Cargill Investor Services and Prudential Securities early buyers, pit sources said.
The premium of futures to cash hog prices to futures and expectations of further losses in cash hog prices Monday, weighed on hog futures.
The IBP cutbacks as well as rolling of long positions into back months weighed on April hog futures, which closed at 74.475 cents per lb versus the latest CME Lean Hog Index at 70.77 cents.

Reports Japan may be keeping its "gate tariff" for frozen pork imports on longer than expected had only minimal effect on the market. Traders noted Japan will still buy ample supplies of U.S. chilled pork.
"We are already exporting a lot of pork to Japan - we're still way up on exports of chilled product," said Dave Maher, livestock analyst for Securities Corporation of Iowa.
E.D.&F. Man and Iowa Grain bought April at the close while Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services bought June. Selling was scattered in April and Refco sold June, pit sources said.
In hog options, trading was very light most of the day with some buying and selling of June 74 puts cited early. Volatility was unchanged, pit sources added.
